title: Keyboard goes dead when the focused part of the window disappears (tree sidebar hidden, filter bar closed by a Smart Folder)
problem: When the focused element is no longer drawn, GPUI dispatches keys and actions to the window root (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/window.rs:6507-6515). It offers `on_focus_lost` to recover (gpui-pre-0.3.10/src/app/context.rs:636), but nothing in src registers it. Every shortcut and menu action is handled on the Finder div under the 'Finder' key context (src/finder/mod.rs:3042-3148), so once focus falls to the root they all stop until a click. Two ways to get there: (1) Tree-mode sidebar. Clicking a row focuses `tree_focus` (src/finder/sidebar.rs:730-732, 861), which is tracked only while the tree is drawn (sidebar.rs:426-430). toggle_sidebar() (mod.rs:2199-2208; Cmd+Alt+S or the Hide Sidebar button) and Sidebar as List (src/finder/folder_tree.rs:524-559) remove it without moving focus. After Cmd+Alt+S, even Cmd+Alt+S can't bring the sidebar back. (2) Filter bar. With the caret in the filter field, clicking a Smart Folder that has no filter sets `filter_open = false` (src/finder/filter.rs:229). The bar disappears (filter.rs:90-92) with focus still in its input. Other closers already fix this by hand: close_filter() (filter.rs:173), the Nushell panel (mod.rs:2627-2631) and tab switches (src/workspace.rs:157-161). The reviewer traced this by reading the code; it has not been run.
proposal: Add one safety net instead of more per-case fixes. src/finder/mod.rs, Finder::new: add to the `subscriptions` vec (501-531) `cx.on_focus_lost(window, |this, window, cx| { if window.focus_lost_restore_target(cx).is_some_and(|h| h == this.focus) { this.focus_files(window, cx); } })`. The browser that held the lost focus hands the keyboard to its own files; hidden tabs and the other pane don't match. src/workspace.rs, Workspace::new: add a fallback `cx.on_focus_lost` that calls `focus_active()` when `window.focus_lost_restore_target(cx)` is None; keep the subscription in the struct. For clarity, also call `focus_files` in toggle_sidebar() and sidebar_mode_changed() when `tree_focus.is_focused(window)`.
original_test_plan: tests/folder_tree.rs: open with `tree_window`, click a tree row and assert `tree_focused`. Press Cmd+Alt+S: assert `show_sidebar` is false and `ui.files_focused()`. Press it again: assert `show_sidebar` is true. This should fail before the fix. tests/controls.rs: add a Smart Folder with no filter through `f.add_smart_folder(..)`. Press Cmd+Alt+F so the filter field has focus, then click (smart, 0). Assert `ui.files_focused()`, and that Cmd+F still focuses the search field.
original_risks: `on_focus_lost` fires for every browser in the window; the restore-target check is what keeps a hidden tab from taking focus. Dialogs and menus keep a focused element, so they don't trigger it. Unverified at runtime, so the new tests should be seen failing first.

verifier.claim_check:
Scenario 1 (tree sidebar) holds; scenario 2 (filter bar closed by a Smart Folder) does not. Traced by reading only; nothing was run.

**Scenario 1 is real.**
- `tree_focus` is tracked only while the tree is drawn: `src/finder/sidebar.rs:426-430`, inside `render_sidebar`, which `src/finder/mod.rs:3173-3175` draws only when `show_sidebar` is true.
- Row clicks focus it (`sidebar.rs:730-732`, `861`, `925-927`).
- `toggle_sidebar` (`mod.rs:2199-2208`) and `sidebar_mode_changed` (`src/finder/folder_tree.rs:550-559`) never move focus.
- No `on_focus_lost`, `on_blur` or `on_focus_out` exists anywhere in `src`, and gpui-kit's Root registers none.
- With the focused id absent from the frame, gpui-pre 0.3.10 dispatches keys and actions from the root node (`window.rs:6507-6515`). Every shortcut is bound in the "Finder" context (`src/actions.rs:129-168`) and handled on the Finder div (`mod.rs:3042-3148`), so none match.
- The Hide Sidebar button triggers it too: Button calls `window.prevent_default()` on mouse-down (gpui-component `button/button.rs:858-866`) and `pill()` stops propagation (`src/finder/toolbar.rs:133`), so the click leaves focus in the tree.
- A path the reviewer missed: `show_sidebar` and `sidebar_mode` are shared settings (`crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:610-613`). `adopt_settings` (`mod.rs:2312-2351`) removes the tree when another window or tab changes them, with no local call site to patch.
- Tree mode is the Windows default (`config.rs:312-315`).
- `docs/manual.md:219` and `:937` and the CHANGELOG do not describe this as intended, and no test pins it. `tests/finder.rs:190-193` toggles with focus in the files; `tests/folder_tree.rs:430-453` switches mode without tree focus.

**Scenario 2 is refuted.**
- The Finder div tracks `self.focus` (`mod.rs:3045`). GPUI focuses the nearest tracked ancestor on mouse-down unless default is prevented (gpui-pre `elements/div.rs:2826-2838`).
- Nothing between a smart row (`sidebar.rs:912-930`) and the Finder div prevents default or stops propagation.
- In list mode, focus has therefore moved from the filter input to `Finder.focus` before the click handler runs `open_smart_folder` (`src/finder/filter.rs:215-237`). In tree mode it has moved to `tree_focus` (`sidebar.rs:426-430`, `925-927`).
- The only other caller is tree keyboard navigation (`folder_tree.rs:932`), where the tree already has focus.
- Focus is never lost here; the "Finder" shortcuts keep working.

**The API the proposal relies on exists.** `Context::on_focus_lost` is at gpui-pre `app/context.rs:636` and `Window::focus_lost_restore_target` at `window.rs:2409`. Focus-lost listeners fire before blur listeners (`window.rs:3540-3567`).
verifier.implementation_notes:
Keep the Finder-level safety net and drop the rest of the proposal.

**1. Add the subscription in `Finder::new`** (`src/finder/mod.rs`, the `subscriptions` vec at 501-531):

```rust
cx.on_focus_lost(window, |this, window, cx| {
    if window.focus_lost_restore_target(cx).is_some_and(|h| h == this.focus) {
        this.focus_files(window, cx);
        cx.defer_in(window, |_, window, _| window.refresh());
    }
}),
```

- **Synchronous focus:** focus the files inside the listener, not deferred. `keyboard_back_from` (`src/finder/inline_rename.rs:184-194`) runs on the later blur event. It then sees the rename input no longer focused and does not refocus a hidden `tree_focus`. This covers a tree rename in progress when the sidebar hides.
- **Deferred refresh:** it is needed. Focus moved inside a focus-lost listener does not schedule a redraw: `Window::focus` suppresses `refresh` during a draw, and `window.rs:3546-3550` resets `focus_before_listeners` so the check at 3579 skips it. Without it the files keep the unfocused selection style (`src/finder/views.rs:547`, `988`) until something else redraws.
- **Strict equality:** keep `h == this.focus`. Do not widen it to `contains`. When an inline-rename field unmounts in the file views or in a still-visible tree, the restore target is `files_focus` or `tree_focus`, so the handler stays out and the existing blur recovery (`inline_rename.rs:153-203`) is untouched.
- **Scope:** only the rendered browser that owned the lost focus matches. Hidden tabs and the other split pane cannot, because their `focus` is not in the frame. `files_focus` is always drawn (`mod.rs:3192`, `3289`), so there is no loop.
- **Also covered:** the cross-window `adopt_settings` case, and a Tab-focused button directly under the Finder div that unmounts.

**2. Drop the `Workspace::new` fallback.**
- Tab and split operations already call `focus_active` (`src/workspace.rs:177`, `186`, `211`, `265`).
- The remaining case where the restore target is None is gpui-component blurring on purpose during a dialog's exit animation and restoring focus on a timer (gpui-component `root.rs:436-445`, `455-487`). A fallback would hand keys to the files mid-animation and call `set_window_title`.
- The tests would not see this, because the harness sets `cx.set_reduce_motion(true)` (`tests/common/mod.rs:193`).

**3. Drop the explicit `focus_files` calls in `toggle_sidebar` and `sidebar_mode_changed`.**
- `set_sidebar_mode(mode, cx)` and `sidebar_mode_changed(cx)` take no `Window`. Adding one changes a public signature used in `dialogs.rs`, `mod.rs:3087-3092`, `tests/common/mod.rs:232` and `tests/folder_tree.rs:26`, `469`.
- They would still miss the `adopt_settings` path.

**4. Drop the filter-bar part.** It is not a focus-loss case. If focus should go to the files after a list-mode sidebar click, that is a separate change (`open_smart_folder` or `navigate` calling `focus_files`), not this fix.

**5. Add a Fixed entry** under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`.
verifier.test_plan:
Add one test to `tests/folder_tree.rs`. It runs headless on Linux. The helpers are already there: `tree_window`, `favorite_ix`, `tree_focused`, `cmd`, and `Ui::{click, press, dispatch, read, files_focused}` from `tests/common/mod.rs`.

1. **Shortcut.** `let (mut ui, _) = tree_window(cx, &fx);` then `ui.click(("fav", favorite_ix(&ui, &fx)))` and assert `tree_focused(&mut ui)`.
   - `ui.press(&cmd("alt-s"))`: assert `!ui.read(|f| f.config().show_sidebar)` and `ui.files_focused()`.
   - `ui.press(&cmd("alt-s"))` again: assert `show_sidebar` is true. Today this second press does nothing, so the test fails first.
2. **Button.** Click the fav row again, then `ui.click("hide-sidebar")`. Assert `ui.files_focused()`, and that `ui.press(&cmd("alt-s"))` shows the sidebar again.
3. **Mode switch.** Click the fav row again, then `ui.dispatch(SidebarAsList)`. Assert `ui.files_focused()`. Then `ui.select(..)` plus `ui.press("down")` to show the file keys work.

Optional guard in `tests/settings.rs`: open with `Open { workspace: true, .. }` and two tabs, lose focus in the active tab, and assert the hidden tab's `files_focused(window)` is false.

Do not add the proposed `tests/controls.rs` Smart Folder test. Focus is never lost there, so it cannot fail first. Its `ui.files_focused()` assertion would also stay false after the fix, because in list mode focus sits on the Finder root.

Existing tests that must stay green:
- `tests/basics.rs:735-772` and `:859-874` (rename field going away)
- `tests/folder_tree.rs:245-290` (keyboard back in the tree after a rename)
- `tests/controls.rs:62-72` and `:1416-1487`
verifier.risks:
Low for the Finder-only handler; nothing here was run, so the new test must be seen failing before the fix.

- **Menus and dialogs are unaffected.** Dialogs render in Root's layer, outside the Finder div, so they never match the restore-target check. PopupMenu restores focus synchronously on dismiss, so it produces no focus-lost frame.
- **Rename-in-tree while the sidebar hides.** The handler runs before the Input's blur event. `end_rename` still commits the typed name, and focus ends in the files instead of on a hidden tree. This is a behaviour change, and an improvement.
- **Stale selection style.** Without the deferred `window.refresh()`, the files keep the unfocused style until another redraw. Tests would not catch that.
- **The Workspace fallback, if kept against this advice,** fires during dialog exit animations, which the reduced-motion test harness hides.
- **Not addressed here.** After a list-mode sidebar click, focus rests on the Finder root, so arrow keys do not reach the files. This is separate, existing behaviour.

orchestrator_notes:
'scope-chips-keep-focus' is on the trunk (read its done record and its commit, 595ce0f): it keeps a click in the search scope bar from taking the keyboard. Its reviewer found the same fault everywhere else, and it belongs with this brief because it is the same family (the keyboard ends up with the browser as a whole, where arrows and typing do nothing). In their words: Found, not fixed (all there before this change).
- After a click on a Smart Folder or any other row of the sidebar's list, and after a click on blank chrome (the status bar, the toolbar's title, the path bar, the filter bar's blank parts), the keyboard is with the browser as a whole: shortcuts work, but arrows and typing do nothing until a file or a field is clicked. This is the fault this brief fixes for the scope bar, everywhere else. Probed for a Smart Folder and the status bar. One fix at the root, such as giving the files the keyboard whenever the Finder's own focus handle gets it, would cover them all; the is_focused half of the test in the bar's listener would then never be true, and the test that pins it would need another way to reach that state.
- A right or middle press on the chrome takes the keyboard away the same way. On an enabled kit Button it gives the keyboard to the button itself, where Return and Space then press it.
- With nothing in the browser holding the keyboard, a menu (Kind, Sort, Actions) gives it back to nothing when it closes. Do this here as a second part, after the plan of record's safety net: when the Finder's own handle gets the keyboard from a press on chrome or a sidebar list row, the files should take it, unless a text field had it and should keep it (look at how 'scope-chips-keep-focus' decides that, and remove the half of its listener that the root fix makes unnecessary only if its tests still pass). Tests that fail today: click a sidebar list row (a Favorite and a Smart Folder), then Down Arrow selects a file; click the status bar or the path bar's blank part, then Down Arrow and type-to-select work; a right press on chrome does not take the keyboard away. Tree mode's sidebar keeps the keyboard in the tree on a click there, as today. If the two parts turn out to pull against each other, do the plan of record, and return the second part as left out with what you learned.
